text: {"standards":[{"code":"L.6.2","verdict":"taught","reason":"In the Literacy Lab 'Edit Like a Detective' and the Learning in Action 'Revise My Own Conclusion and Draft' activity, students check capitalization, punctuation, spelling, and agreement in their own draft paragraph."},{"code":"L.6.2.a","verdict":"taught","reason":"The 'Edit Like a Detective' activity teaches students to recognize an extra element and set it off with commas, and students then find and punctuate an extra element in their own paragraph; parentheses and dashes are named but get less practice."},{"code":"L.6.2.b","verdict":"partly","reason":"Spelling appears only as a brief direction to use a dictionary or spell check and a passing reminder to check spelling of mythological names, with no instruction or practice in spelling words correctly."},{"code":"W.6.5","verdict":"taught","reason":"Students revise their conclusions and drafts in 'Revise My Own Conclusion and Draft' and give and use partner feedback in 'Structured Peer Feedback', with teacher modeling in the think-aloud."}],"anchorText":{"verdict":"partly","reason":"The Lightning Thief appears only as an incidental example in the teacher's model conclusion and a capitalization note, while the Outline's example essay is described as teacher-provided or from Lesson 36 and no pages are named or used."}}
